messages:
amir: Hey all, joining from a mobile hotspot on my phone today. WireGuard says connected but I can't access our internal file share (SMB) at 10.45.20.5. Finder times out. I can ssh to the bastion though. Any hotspot-specific quirks?
julia: welcome! :wave: mobile hotspots often put you behind CGNAT and block peer-to-peer traffic which breaks some internal protocols (SMB uses ephemeral ports). Does `smbclient -L //10.45.20.5 -N` from terminal show anything?
amir: `smbclient` just hangs. `ping 10.45.20.5` works over wg0. `netstat -an | grep 445` shows nothing local.
netops: ping working but SMB hanging smells like UDP/TCP fragmentation or carrier NAT interfering with large packets. Two quick options:
1) Mount via SSHFS over the bastion: `ssh -J amir@bastion-eu-1 -oCompression=no -oServerAliveInterval=60 amir@internal-filehost 'tar -cf - /exports/myhome' | tar -xvf - -C ~/work` (quick copy workaround)
2) Use an SSH local port forward for SMB over TCP: `ssh -L 1445:10.45.20.5:445 amir@bastion-eu-1` then connect to `localhost:1445` as smb target.
3) If you want a persistent mount: `sshfs -o workaround=all amir@bastion-eu-1:/exports/myhome ~/mnt` (performance varies).
amir: tried ssh -L 1445... then `smbclient -L //localhost:1445 -N` gives a listing! Nice.
bastion-bot: user/amir provisioned on bastion-eu-1
netops: great. Follow-ups: if you plan to use hotspot regularly, set WG MTU to 1280 to avoid fragmentation: `sudo ip link set dev wg0 mtu 1280`. Also consider using `MSSClamp` we can enable server-side (ticketed) to help TCP-through-UDP tunnels.
amir: set mtu 1280 and tested direct smbclient to 10.45.20.5 again — still flaky unless via the SSH tunnel, so hotspot is probably doing some stateful filtering.
julia (typo): it-support: can we add a note on recommended SSH port-forward pattern for SMB for mobile hotspots in onboarding?
it-support: opened ONB-789: "Mobile hotspot / CGNAT: SSH tunnel patterns for accessing internal SMB/NFS" assigned to netops. We'll add examples: `ssh -L` and `sshfs` and mention MTU 1280 for hotspots.
julia: one more tip — for mac users you can map a Finder shortcut using `localhost:1445` once the tunnel is up, or use `mount_smbfs //user@localhost:1445/share ~/mnt` on mac.
amir: that worked for Finder after creating the SSH tunnel. Thanks, everyone! I'll paste the exact commands into my onboarding notes. :tada:
netops: thanks for reporting — we'll add a short hotspot troubleshooting bullet to the new-hires doc with commands and the ticket link.
